title: Choosing Arrays, Strings and Vectors
learningObjectives: Explain choosing arrays, strings and vectors.
Describe relevant storage, indexing and size rules.
Trace a collection operation or traversal.
Recognize bounds, lifetime or input pitfalls.
Apply the type to a practical collection task.

understand.concept: Raw arrays, std::array, std::string and std::vector differ in fixed/dynamic size, text semantics and interfaces.
understand.whyItMatters: Choosing a container makes code safer and clearer.
understand.explain: Prefer standard containers; choose based on fixed size, dynamic size, or text.

examples.explanation: These collections have different size behavior and interfaces.

examples.explanation: string manages text; char array is null-terminated.

examples.title: Read-only traversal
examples.explanation: Use range-for when no index is required.

practise.guidedTask: Trace all five Choosing Arrays, Strings and Vectors examples. Record sizes, indexes, values and condition checks. Identify first/last valid element and relevant edge cases.
practise.independentTask: Create a small C++ data-processing program demonstrating choosing arrays, strings and vectors. Test typical values, empty/boundary cases, and invalid input or indexing where relevant. Explain why this collection is appropriate.
hints: Use zero-based indexes and verify bounds.
Prefer range-based traversal when index is unnecessary.
Check emptiness before operations such as front or pop_back.
Test first, last and invalid boundaries.
